# Tool reference

Every tool works the same from the CLI (`engram <tool> key=value`), over MCP
(`engram_<tool>` in most agents) and on the daemon socket. Tools marked
**approval** wait for the user's decision in the Engram window when an agent calls them.

## Target and process

### `status`

Session overview: target, scan, table, permissions, next-step hints

Call first in every session and whenever unsure. Returns the attached process (if any), the current scan (types and candidate counts), the address table, the write-approval policy, whether the GUI is open, and `hints` with suggested next steps.

```sh
engram status '{}'
```

### `processes`

List the user's processes (games first); Wine/Proton aware

Lists processes owned by the user, largest memory first. Wine/Proton games appear under their Windows name (Game.exe) with kind=proton and steam_app_id. Runtime helpers (wineserver, services.exe, pressure-vessel, ...) are hidden unless include_helpers=true. Use `query` to filter by name or command line, then attach by pid.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_helpers` | boolean | `false` |  |
| `limit` | integer | `25` |  |
| `query` | string |  | Case-insensitive substring of name/cmdline |

```sh
engram processes '{"query":"minecraft"}'
```

### `attach`

Select the target process by pid or unique name

Selects the process all other tools operate on. Engram does not stop the process. Only processes of the same user can be attached. If several processes match `name`, the call fails and lists them: ask the user which one. Loads the saved address table for this game.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | Unique case-insensitive substring of the process name |
| `pid` | integer |  |  |

```sh
engram attach '{"pid":12345}'
```

### `detach`

Forget the target (stops freezes, clears the scan)

Releases the target. Frozen entries stop being written.

```sh
engram detach '{}'
```

### `process_control` · **approval**

Pause or resume the target (SIGSTOP/SIGCONT)

Freezes the game for consistent multi-step edits. Always resume afterwards.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | required |  |

```sh
engram process_control '{"action":"pause"}'
```

### `launch` · **approval**

Start a program as a child of Engram (traceable without extra privileges)

Starts argv with Engram as its parent, which lets Engram read its memory even when the kernel restricts ptrace (Yama) and Engram has no capability. Prefer asking the user; most setups use attach.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `argv` | array | required |  |
| `cwd` | string |  |  |
| `env` | object |  |  |

```sh
engram launch '{"argv":["/usr/bin/supertuxkart"]}'
```

## Value scans

### `scan`

Start a new value scan (exact/unknown/range); type=auto tries several types

Starts a NEW scan (replacing the previous one) over writable memory. compare: exact | unknown | greater | less | between | not_equal. type: auto (default: tries i32,i64,f32,f64 at once and ranks candidates), a numeric type, or bytes (array-of-bytes pattern with ?? wildcards), string, string16 (UTF-16, common in Unity/.NET). Floats match with rounding to the digits given ("100" matches 99.5..100.5). Typical flow: scan value=<number the game shows> -> ask the user to change it in-game -> scan_next. Returns counts per type and the best-ranked candidates.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aligned` | boolean | `true` |  |
| `compare` | string | `"exact"` |  |
| `limit` | integer | `15` | Candidates to return |
| `module` | string |  | Restrict to one module's address range |
| `type` | string | `"auto"` | auto \| i8..i64 \| u8..u64 \| f32 \| f64 \| bytes \| string \| string16 |
| `value` | string |  | Value to look for (not needed for unknown) |
| `value2` | string |  | Upper bound for between |
| `writable_only` | boolean | `true` |  |

```sh
engram scan '{"value":"37"}'
```

### `scan_next`

Narrow the current scan after the value changed in-game

Filters the current candidates against fresh memory. compare: exact (value) | changed | unchanged | increased | decreased | increased_by (value) | decreased_by (value) | greater | less | between | not_equal. Before calling, the user must have changed the value in-game (or deliberately not, for unchanged). Usually 2-4 rounds reach a handful of candidates.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `compare` | string | `"exact"` |  |
| `limit` | integer | `15` |  |
| `value` | string |  |  |
| `value2` | string |  |  |

```sh
engram scan_next '{"compare":"exact","value":"36"}'
```

### `scan_results`

Page through scan candidates with current and previous values

Lists candidates in address order with live values. Use `type` to see one type of a multi-type scan.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | `50` |  |
| `offset` | integer | `0` |  |
| `type` | string |  |  |

```sh
engram scan_results '{"limit":20}'
```

### `scan_undo`

Revert the last scan_next

Restores the candidate set from before the last scan_next (one level).

```sh
engram scan_undo '{}'
```

### `scan_reset`

Drop the current scan

Frees the scan session memory.

```sh
engram scan_reset '{}'
```

### `cancel`

Cancel a running scan or pointer scan

Asks a long-running scan to stop early.

```sh
engram cancel '{}'
```

## Address table

### `table_list`

The address table (saved cheats) with live values

Entries the user or agent saved: id, description, address expression, type, live value, frozen. The table is saved per game and reloaded on attach.

```sh
engram table_list '{}'
```

### `table_add`

Save an address to the table (visible and editable in the GUI)

Adds an entry the user can see and edit. Use a clear description ("Gold", "Player health"). Prefer a pointer-path expression from pointer_scan when available so it survives restarts.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `type` | string | `"i32"` | Data type (i8 i16 i32 i64 u8 u16 u32 u64 f32 f64 ptr bytes:N str:N str16:N). Default i32. |

```sh
engram table_add '{"address":"0x7f12a0","type":"i32","description":"Gold"}'
```

### `table_set` · **approval**

Edit a table entry: value, freeze, description, address, type

Setting `value` writes memory and `freeze`=true keeps rewriting the value (10x per second); both need user approval when called by an agent. Changing `address` to a pointer path makes the entry durable.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string |  | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `freeze` | boolean |  |  |
| `id` | integer | required |  |
| `reason` | string |  | Shown to the user in the approval prompt |
| `type` | string |  |  |
| `value` | string |  |  |

```sh
engram table_set '{"id":1,"freeze":true,"reason":"Infinite health"}'
```

### `table_remove`

Remove a table entry

Deletes an entry (and its freeze).

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | required |  |

```sh
engram table_remove '{"id":3}'
```

## Memory

### `modules`

Loaded modules (ELF .so / PE .exe/.dll) with base addresses

Modules of the target with base and size. For Proton games the game's .exe and .dll files appear here; use their names in address expressions (Game.exe+0x1234).

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | `40` |  |
| `query` | string |  |  |

```sh
engram modules '{"query":".exe"}'
```

### `regions`

Memory map summary (heap/stack/anon/image regions)

Memory regions of the target with permissions and kind. Mostly useful to understand where an address lives; `analyze` already explains single addresses.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string |  |  |
| `limit` | integer | `50` |  |
| `writable_only` | boolean | `false` |  |

```sh
engram regions '{"writable_only":true,"limit":20}'
```

### `read`

Read typed values at an address

Reads `count` consecutive values of `type` starting at `address`. Works while the game runs.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |
| `count` | integer | `1` |  |
| `type` | string | `"i32"` | Data type (i8 i16 i32 i64 u8 u16 u32 u64 f32 f64 ptr bytes:N str:N str16:N). Default i32. |

```sh
engram read '{"address":"0x7f1234560010","type":"f32","count":3}'
```

### `hexdump`

Hex + ASCII dump of memory

Classic 16-bytes-per-line dump. Prefer `dissect` for understanding structures.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |
| `size` | integer | `256` |  |

```sh
engram hexdump '{"address":"Game.exe+0x1000","size":64}'
```

### `write` · **approval**

Write a typed value (needs user approval for agents)

Writes `value` as `type` at `address`. ALWAYS pass `expected` (the value you just read) so a stale address is rejected instead of corrupting memory, and a human-readable `reason` the user sees in the approval prompt. Read the value back afterwards and ask the user to confirm the in-game effect.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |
| `expected` | string |  | Current value; the write is refused if memory differs |
| `reason` | string |  | Shown to the user, e.g. 'Double gold: 150 -> 300' |
| `type` | string | `"i32"` | Data type (i8 i16 i32 i64 u8 u16 u32 u64 f32 f64 ptr bytes:N str:N str16:N). Default i32. |
| `value` | string | required | New value, formatted for the type ("200", "1.5", "90 90", "text") |

```sh
engram write '{"address":"0x7f12a0","type":"i32","value":"300","expected":"150","reason":"Double gold"}'
```

## Analysis

### `analyze`

Explain an address: region, module+offset, all type interpretations, pointer target, text

One call to understand what an address is: which mapping it is in (heap/stack/image), module+offset, the bytes interpreted as every numeric type, whether it looks like a pointer (and to where) or a string. Use it to sanity-check scan candidates before writing.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |

```sh
engram analyze '{"address":"0x7f12a0"}'
```

### `dissect`

Guess the structure around an address (pointers, floats, ints, strings)

Heuristically types each field in `size` bytes starting at `address`: pointers (with targets), floats, ints, zero runs and text. Start a bit before a found value (address-0x40) to see its neighbours: related stats (max health, ammo in clip/reserve, position x/y/z) usually sit in the same object.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |
| `size` | integer | `128` |  |

```sh
engram dissect '{"address":"0x7f12a0-0x40","size":192}'
```

### `pointer_scan`

Find stable pointer paths (module+offset chains) to an address

Searches chains like [[Game.exe+0x1A2B30]+0x18]+0x40 that end at `address`, so the value can be found again after the game restarts. Takes seconds to a minute on big games. Best results: pass the address of a value you already verified. Store the winning `expr` with table_set address=<expr>.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |
| `limit` | integer | `10` |  |
| `max_depth` | integer | `3` |  |
| `max_offset` | string | `"0x1000"` | Max offset per level (hex) |

```sh
engram pointer_scan '{"address":"0x7f12a0"}'
```

### `disassemble`

Disassemble x86/x64 code (Intel syntax)

Decodes `count` instructions at `address`, with module+offset locations.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |
| `count` | integer | `16` |  |

```sh
engram disassemble '{"address":"Game.exe+0x4f2a0","count":12}'
```

### `watch` · **approval**

Find the code that writes/accesses an address (hardware watchpoint)

Arms a CPU debug-register watchpoint on every thread for `duration_ms`, while the user triggers the change in-game (tell them to before calling!). Returns each instruction that wrote/accessed the address with hit count and the registers at the first hit. Useful to find the struct base register (e.g. rcx+0x18) or code to patch. Briefly traces the game; needs user approval for agents.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |
| `duration_ms` | integer | `5000` |  |
| `kind` | string | `"write"` |  |
| `max_hits` | integer | `2000` |  |
| `size` | integer | `4` |  |

```sh
engram watch '{"address":"0x7f12a0","kind":"write","duration_ms":6000}'
```

### `sample`

Record a value over time (observe how it changes)

Reads `address` `samples` times every `interval_ms` and returns the series plus min/max/changes. Good for telling a timer from a counter, or checking a candidate reacts to gameplay.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | Address expression: hex (0x7f12ab30), module+offset (Game.exe+0x1A2B30) or pointer path ([[Game.exe+0x10]+0x18]+0x40). |
| `interval_ms` | integer | `250` |  |
| `samples` | integer | `10` |  |
| `type` | string | `"i32"` | Data type (i8 i16 i32 i64 u8 u16 u32 u64 f32 f64 ptr bytes:N str:N str16:N). Default i32. |

```sh
engram sample '{"address":"0x7f12a0","type":"f32","samples":20,"interval_ms":100}'
```

## Talking to the user

### `notify`

Show a message to the user in the Engram window

Posts a message in the GUI activity feed (e.g. 'Found gold at Game.exe+0x1234, added to table').

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | string | `"info"` |  |
| `message` | string | required |  |

```sh
engram notify '{"message":"Gold found and added to the table","level":"success"}'
```
